title: Merul Badda flooding: a detailed monsoon guide
body:
Every year people ask whether Merul Badda floods, so here is a detailed write-up after two monsoons living on the lane behind the BRAC University campus.

The worst part is the Link Road stretch between the campus and the Badda main road. After 30 minutes of heavy rain the water reaches ankle height, and after an hour it can reach the knee near the drain that is always clogged. Rickshaw pullers charge 60 to 80 taka for a ride that normally costs 20.

Ground floor flats on the inner lanes get water inside the stairwell two or three times each season. If you are renting, ask for the first floor or above, and check if the building has a raised entrance step.

The water usually drains within four to six hours. Classes rarely get cancelled, so plan to carry spare socks and keep your laptop in a waterproof bag in June and July.

The upside: rent here is cheaper than Gulshan or Banani by almost half, and you can walk to campus in ten minutes on dry days. I would still choose Merul Badda, just not a ground floor flat.

body:

Utilities: Gas line was reliable. No flooding problems in my lane.

Overall it's okay, but I would look at nearby areas first.
